items.caseName: K. Ravi Shankar v. Basai Steels and Power Private Limited & Anr.
items.caseNo: IA (CAA) No. 150 of 2026 in CP (CAA) No. 30/230/HDB/2026
items.coram: Rajeev Bhardwaj (Judicial Member) and Sanjay Puri (Technical Member)
items.headline: NCLT Hyderabad: Inherent powers cannot waive 10% shareholding threshold to object to amalgamation scheme
items.text: A shareholder holding about 8.5% of Basai Steels and Power challenged the 1:413 share-exchange ratio in a proposed amalgamation and sought fresh valuation. The Tribunal held that the 10% threshold in the proviso to Section 230(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 is an objective test that cannot be relaxed under Rule 11 of the NCLT Rules, and refused to club the holdings of the late shareholder's legal heirs who were not before it. The objection was dismissed as not maintainable without going into the merits.

items.headline: ITAT Jaipur upholds Rs 1.51 lakh Section 80GGC disallowance: NEFT payment and receipt alone do not prove genuine political donation
items.text: The assessee claimed a Section 80GGC deduction for an NEFT contribution to Rashtriya Samajwadi Party (Secular) for AY 2019-20; the case was reopened after a September 2022 search on registered unrecognised political parties. Relying on statements of party office-bearers that donations were returned in cash after deducting commission, the Tribunal held that a bank transfer and donation receipt by themselves do not establish a genuine contribution and upheld the disallowance.
